subject: general
question: The power of a test is:
solution:
The power of a test is **1 - P(Type II error).**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **1 - P(Type II error):**

 
 
• The power of a test is defined as the probability that the test correctly rejects the null hypothesis when the alternative hypothesis is true. It is calculated as 1 minus the probability of a Type II error (β).
 
• In a financial enterprise context, having a high power in tests such as credit risk assessments or fraud detection means accurately identifying true positives, thereby minimizing potential financial losses.
 
• Improving the power of a test can involve increasing the sample size, choosing more effective test statistics, or improving data quality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **P(Type I error):**

 
 
• This is the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true, also known as the significance level (α). While important in hypothesis testing, it does not define the power of a test.
 
 
 
• **P(Type II error):**
 
 
• This is the probability of failing to reject the null hypothesis when the alternative hypothesis is true. It is denoted by β. The power of a test is inversely related to this probability but not equal to it.
 
 
 
• **1 - P(Type I error):**
 
 
• This represents the probability of not making a Type I error, but it does not relate to the power of the test. It is more about the test's ability to avoid false positives.
